report_name: Polymarket Hacked via Compromised DebugBear RUM Script

attack_patterns.name: Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools
attack_patterns.description: The attack originated from a compromised third-party script from DebugBear, a software dependency for Polymarket's website.

attack_patterns.name: JavaScript
attack_patterns.description: Malicious JavaScript was injected into DebugBear's Real User Monitoring (RUM) script to hijack user sessions and execute unauthorized transactions.

attack_patterns.name: Drive-by Compromise
attack_patterns.description: Polymarket users were compromised by visiting the legitimate website, which then loaded the malicious third-party script from DebugBear.

attack_patterns.name: Resource Hijacking
attack_patterns.description: The attack hijacked authenticated user sessions and their associated financial resources, liquidating positions and transferring funds to attacker-controlled wallets.

attack_patterns.name: Browser Session Hijacking
attack_patterns.description: The malicious script used the existing authenticated user session's authority to interact with Polymarket's trading functions without needing to steal credentials.

malware.name: Malicious JavaScript
malware.description: A malicious JavaScript payload injected into the DebugBear RUM script, designed to hijack active user sessions on Polymarket to liquidate positions and exfiltrate funds.

tools.name: DebugBear RUM Script
tools.description: A legitimate Real User Monitoring (RUM) script from DebugBear that was compromised by attackers and used to deliver malicious JavaScript to Polymarket users.

identities.name: Polymarket
identities.description: A prediction market platform that was the target of a supply chain attack, resulting in the theft of $2.71 million from its users' accounts.

identities.name: DebugBear
identities.description: A website performance monitoring firm whose Real User Monitoring (RUM) script was compromised and used as the vector for the supply chain attack against Polymarket.

infrastructure.name: DebugBear Script Hosting Infrastructure
infrastructure.description: The infrastructure belonging to DebugBear that was compromised by attackers to host and serve the malicious version of the 'rum.js' script.

indicators.name: Compromised RUM Script File Detection
indicators.x_netsecio_sigma_rule:
title: Compromised DebugBear RUM Script File
id: 4b9c1d8e-7f6a-4b1c-8d9e-0f1a2b3c4d5e
status: experimental
description: Detects the presence of 'rum.js', which was compromised in the Polymarket supply chain attack. This rule is broad and requires tuning to focus on unexpected locations or hashes.
references:
  - https://www.securityweek.com/2-million-drained-from-polymarket-traders-in-new-supply-chain-attack/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-30
tags:
  - attack.t1195.001
level: medium
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|endswith: '\rum.js'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the presence of the 'rum.js' file, which was the vehicle for the supply chain attack.

indicators.name: Suspicious RUM Script Web Request
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious RUM Script Web Request
id: 5c8a3b2d-1e9f-4a0b-9c8d-7e6f5d4c3b2a
status: experimental
description: Detects web requests for rum.js. This script was compromised in the Polymarket supply chain attack. Legitimate requests are expected, but this can be used to monitor for unexpected script loading or modifications when combined with other analytics like file integrity monitoring.
references:
  - https://www.securityweek.com/2-million-drained-from-polymarket-traders-in-new-supply-chain-attack/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-30
tags:
  - attack.t1189
level: low
logsource:
  category: proxy
detection:
  selection:
    c-uri|endswith: '/rum.js'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects web requests for 'rum.js', the script that was compromised in the attack. This could indicate a site loading the potentially malicious script.
